input.summary:
West ground corridor: two standing lanterns at x31 and x38 on z51 (north side, clear of the doorways and the z52 lane) are written in parts/room-4.mjs build(g). A scratch copy with the lock bypassed checks OK: min 9, 0 dark, 34/34 reachable.
In the real merged build, runParts refuses both lantern writes because the mansion shell carves the corridor to owned air, so the room still reads NEEDS WORK (min 0, 28 dark, 6 dim). The part is not finished.
The build.nbt still wrote successfully (make.sh exit 0), but it has no corridor light.
left: BLOCKER (not mine to change): parts/shell.mjs fills the room interiors with "air" (carve, around line 27), and build.mjs runParts (~line 220) treats every cell an earlier part wrote, air included, as owned. Lamps in the corridor air are refused: 'REFUSED 2 writes ... 31,4,51 lantern air; 38,4,51 lantern air'. Fix options for the shell/library owner: leave room interiors unowned (air the shell does not 'write'), or give a lighting part an explicit allowance into air. I did not edit the shell or the library, per 'touch nothing else'.
Once the lock allows it, the existing build(g) lamp code should land as is. Re-run ./make.sh and `mcd room build.nbt --rooms rooms.json --only "west ground corridor"`; expect OK with min 9.

Designer note mismatch: the note names a console lantern and an x42 hanging lantern as the main sources. The merged room has neither: build(g) is empty, the console and lit candle are refused (parked), and the designer's hanging lanterns sit at x28/32/36/40 in the unused LAYERS const. My lamps do not depend on the console, and they do not sit in its footprint (x33..35) or on the barrel (x28).
Scratch files are in /tmp/lamp-scratch-w4 (scratch.mjs, in.nbt, lit.nbt), outside the run directory.

waste.what: Worked out each lamp's light by hand, cell by cell (Manhattan falloff from a 15-level source) to pick the lantern spots, then found the lock by building and reading refusals one run at a time.
waste.cost: about 3 full ./make.sh cycles, plus a failed sed edit (BSD sed needs -i '') and a missing import that broke the build once
waste.tool: `mcd room --try-lamps x,y,z ...` (or runParts reporting 'cell owned by <part>' ahead of time) would have answered in one call whether a lamp cell is writable and what light it gives. A `mcd light` option to test candidate lamps on a scratch copy with the lock off would have skipped the trial builds.

waste.what: Made a scratch copy of the build with the candidate lanterns added directly (lock bypassed) to verify the plan, since the lock blocked the real placement.
waste.cost: one small scratch script plus two room checks
waste.tool: A `--scratch` mode on `mcd room` / `mcd light` that reads a build and reports light for hypothetical blocks would make this a single command.

companions.task: Own the mansion shell's corridor air (parts/shell.mjs, the room interiors filled with air). Either leave interior air unowned so later fittings can be placed, or mark it as carved-but-open, so the lamplighter's two lanterns at x31 and x38 on z51 (and the designer's console and hanging lanterns) can land.
